verdict.rationale: Maritime documents that every API key carries scopes and recommends handing each subsystem the narrowest key it needs. It gives a concrete least-privilege example: a Computers-only key is refused on every other endpoint. Missing for 10: a documented list of available scopes beyond `computers`, key expiry/rotation controls (keys are documented as never expiring), per-agent scoping detail, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Every key carries scopes. Hand a subsystem the _narrowest_ key it needs. A leaked key can then only do what its scope allows.
To hand out a key that reaches computers and nothing else, create a **Computers key** in the Computers section of Settings, API keys
a key whose only scope is `computers` is refused on every other Maritime endpoint
